review_notes: I read the whole file, including the S04V valuation helpers, the Frame section, and the IdentCore and IdentFrame sections. The only simp attributes are the five `@[scoped simp]` frame_a_i lemmas. I checked Mathlib's `WeierstrassCurve.map` (`@[simps]`, which generates the simp lemmas `map_a₁` and so on) and `baseChange`. I also read the Mathlib note that `negY` is deliberately not unfolded by simp; `frame_negY` is correctly left non-simp and is used by explicit `rw` or `simp only`. I did not run Lean, so I don't know whether the redundant simp rules actually conflict in practice. The finding is therefore about redundancy and an unneeded global attribute, not an observed failure. I found nothing else that needs a simp annotation or has a bad orientation.

findings.declaration: frame_a₁ / frame_a₂ / frame_a₃ / frame_a₄ / frame_a₆ (the `@[scoped simp]` attributes)
findings.excerpt: @[scoped simp] lemma frame_a₁ : ((W.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ))⁄Qb).toAffine.a₁ = (W.a₁ : Qb) := by simp
findings.problem: Each of these five lemmas is proved by plain `simp`. That means Mathlib's default simp set (the `@[simps]` lemmas `WeierstrassCurve.map_a₁` etc., followed by the integer-cast and `algebraMap` simp lemmas) already rewrites the left-hand side to the stated normal form. Adding `scoped simp` registers a second, overlapping rule on the same head symbol `WeierstrassCurve.a₁` (and `a₂`, `a₃`, `a₄`, `a₆`) of the same term. The left-hand side is not in simp-normal form, so the rule is redundant with the existing `map_a_i` chain. It also adds a file-specific rule to the global simp set whenever the namespace is open. The lemmas are only needed as named rewrite rules: the file uses them in `simp only [addX, frame_a₁, frame_a₂, frame_a₄, ...]` at lines 360 and 399, and for that the `simp` attribute is not needed.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `scoped simp` from all five lemmas and keep them as plain lemmas, since they are cited by name in `simp only [...]`. Alternatively, drop the five lemmas and use `simp only [WeierstrassCurve.map_a₁, ...]` followed by the cast simp lemmas. If a simp lemma is wanted, state it in the canonical orientation for the existing normal form, so it doesn't overlap `map_a_i`.
findings.benefit: A reader no longer has to wonder whether these rules compete with, or are dead next to, Mathlib's `map_a_i` simp lemmas. The simp set stays predictable: the only explicit uses are the `simp only` calls, which don't depend on the attribute. Unnecessary scoped simp rules, which could slow down or alter other `simp` calls when the namespace is opened, are removed.
